column2: On the authority of Anas ibn Mālik (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Allah the Exalted said:

O son of Ādam, as long as you call upon Me and hope in Me, I will forgive you for whatever you have done, and I do not mind. O son of Ādam, if your sins were to reach the clouds of the sky and you then sought My forgiveness, I would forgive you.

O son of Ādam, if you were to come to Me with sins nearly filling the earth, and then meet Me without associating anything with Me, I would come to you with forgiveness nearly filling it.” Reported by al-Tirmidhī, who said: An authentic hadith.

Mā daʿawtanī (“as long as you call upon Me”): so that I forgive you your sins; mā is adverbial and verbal. Wa-rajawtanī (“and hope in Me”): you hope for My mercy and pardon. Ghafartu laka (“I will forgive you”): your sins, by covering and erasing them.
“For whatever you have done”: of repeated sins. Wa-lā ubālī (“and I do not mind”): I do not deem your sins too many.

ʿAnān al-samāʾ (“the clouds of the sky”): the clouds. Istaghfartanī (“you sought My forgiveness”): you asked Me for forgiveness. Bi-qurāb al-arḍ (“nearly filling the earth”): what nearly fills it. Laqītanī (“meet Me”): die upon faith. “Without associating anything with Me”: in tawḥīd and worship. La-ataytuka (“I would come to you”): I would give you a great forgiveness nearly filling the earth.

The vastness of Allah's favour, generosity and munificence to His servants: when a servant sins, repents of his sins and then asks Allah to erase them, Allah, Glorified is He, forgives them, however many they are.
Whoever dies without associating anything with Allah may hope to enter Paradise.
A human being is not protected from sins, but when he sins and calls upon Allah, his supplication is accepted and his sin forgiven.
This hadith is a refutation of the Khawārij and the Muʿtazilah, who declare a Muslim a disbeliever on account of sins.

This hadith contains good news for the Muslims, for it shows the vastness of Allah's mercy, generosity, munificence and favour to His servants: whoever commits great sins and then asks Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He,

and hopes in Him and does not despair of His mercy, Allah the Exalted forgives his sins, however many they are, if he seeks Allah's forgiveness without associating anything with Allah: “Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills” [al-Nisāʾ 4:48];

“O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful” [al-Zumar 39:53]. The poet said on this:
When my heart grew hard and my ways grew narrow, / I made my hope a ladder towards Your pardon.
My sin seemed enormous to me, but when I compared it / with Your pardon, my Lord, Your pardon was greater.
